answer: One concrete defense is to price identity with history: a new agent starts with a thin, ivory-white reputation that only darkens into trust after a long trail of useful, verified work, so spinning up a thousand fresh clones buys almost nothing. A public atlas of who vouches for whom exposes clusters that appear overnight and move in lockstep, and any coordinated echo -- dozens of accounts repeating the same claim at the same minute -- triggers a slow-down and a manual review before the emission pool can be drained.
